summary.oneLiner: Ola Electric achieved its first operating cash flow positive quarter (₹91cr CFO) driven by a structural gross margin expansion to 38.5% and a 50% YoY OpEx reset, validating the Gen 3 platform economics. With breakeven lowered to 20k-25k units/month and a visible order backlog, the company is pivoting from survival to scaling its integrated auto-cell-energy stack without significant incremental CapEx.

one-line thesis: Ola Electric achieved its first operating cash flow positive quarter (₹91cr CFO) driven by a structural gross margin expansion to 38.5% and a 50% YoY OpEx reset, validating the Gen 3 platform economics. With breakeven lowered to 20k-25k units/month and a visible order backlog, the company is pivoting from survival to scaling its integrated auto-cell-energy stack without significant incremental CapEx.
financial scorecard: Revenue: ₹2,253cr (FY26 Consolidated), Q4 impacted by low deliveries; EBITDA/Margin: Gross Margin 38.5% (Q4), 33.5% ex-PLI; PAT: Not explicitly disclosed but moving towards breakeven at 20-25k units; Order Book: Auto backlog present, inventory days down to 3-4; Net Debt: Not detailed, but FCF positive in Auto segment (₹173cr in Q4); One-offs: ₹20-30cr revenue hit due to one-time accounting change deferring extended warranty recognition.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Q1FY27 rev ₹500-550cr (nearly double Q4); Margin: Hold industry-leading GM >35%; Order Inflow: 40k-45k orders expected in Q1FY27; Capex: Auto maintenance ~₹50cr/yr, Cell Capex for 6GWh completing in Q1/Q2 FY27, no further major CapEx until subsidiary fundraising.
order book & pipeline: Production backlog exists due to supply chain ramp; Inventory days reduced to 3-4 days; April registrations up 20% MoM despite industry decline; May trending 14k-15k registrations.
segment / subsidiary detail: Auto: Near FCF positive, 1Mn unit capacity ready, Gen 3 warranty costs down to ₹59cr (from ₹500cr+); Cell: 2.5GWh operational, 6GWh commissioning by June, 15% of vehicles now use Bharat Cells, targeting 10-15% cost advantage at scale.
growth verticals / optionality: Roadster (EV Bike) contributing 15% of orders with 50%+ segment share; Shakti (B2B storage) ramping post-auto allocation; Mahashakti (Grid) in development; External cell sales pipeline emerging.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin 38.5% (structural via vertical integration); OpEx reset from ₹844cr (Q4FY25) to ₹428cr (Q4FY26), targeting ₹300-350cr run-rate; Warranty costs reduced 88% YoY.
capex / expansion: Auto Capex largely complete (maintenance only ~₹50cr/yr); Gigafactory 6GWh Capex concluding Q1/Q2 FY27; Future 20GWh expansion to be funded via subsidiary equity raise.
capital allocation: Priority 1: Ramp Gigafactory for captive auto use; Priority 2: Scale Shakti/Mahashakti; Priority 3: Raise separate capital for Cell subsidiary expansion beyond 6GWh.
risks & watch-items: Supply chain ramp speed to clear backlog; Commodity price volatility (Lithium upcycle); Execution risk on 6GWh yield stabilization; Regulatory shifts in PLI/ACC schemes.
management quality / tone: Confident, turnaround-focused, emphasizing 'structural advantages' and 'operating leverage'; transparent on past service issues now resolved.
non-obvious takeaways: 90%+ of OpEx is fixed, creating massive operating leverage as volumes rebound; Accounting change on warranty revenue recognition created a one-time ₹20-30cr drag but improves future visibility; EV Bike segment tripling in size with Ola holding 50%+ share.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising lithium prices and import dependency | Ola Electric Mobility Ltd | beneficiary | High | Vertical integration with own Gigafactory provides 10-15% cost advantage and insulation from global cell shortages. |
| Service network inefficiencies hurting brand | Ola Electric Mobility Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Service backlogs down 88%, same-day closure at 87%, driving V-shaped volume recovery. |
| High CapEx intensity in EV manufacturing | Competitors lacking cell integration | loser | High | Competitors face new CapEx cycles for cells while Ola's asset base supports ₹15k-20k cr revenue without incremental spend. |

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

themes.title: EV-OEM & domestic cell manufacturing
themes.need: Domestic EV OEMs and cell/Gigafactory localization (PLI) are scaling unit volumes and chasing battery cost-downs to reach profitability. The binding question is cell-to-pack localization and vehicle-volume ramp, distinct from Tier-1 component supply.
themes.driver: Vehicle-volume ramp + Gigafactory/PLI cell localization & improving EV-OEM unit economics.
